title: Quick-Compare Panel + Onboard Wizard for model version selection
creator: Amina Patel
description: Introduce a compact Quick-Compare Panel in the Console's Model Picker that surfaces performance profile deltas and a short onboarding wizard to help engineers pin a safe version during initial onboarding. The goal is to reduce time-to-pin for new models, surface risky regressions early, and provide actionable pin suggestions based on traffic profile matches and latency/cost trade-offs.
background: Current model version selection flow requires users to open multiple tabs (profiles, benchmarks, previous pins) and manually reconcile metrics — this is error-prone and slows onboarding.
PM hypothesis: a contextual, side-by-side micro-dashboard + guided wizard will improve successful pins on first attempt and reduce rollback rate.

Scope: Console UX only (no runtime changes). Will rely on existing perf profile API and metrics tiles exposed by the Console backend. Edge cases for private on-prem builds should be considered but deprioritized for first rollout.
acceptance_criteria: A Quick-Compare Panel is available from the Model Picker when a user hovers or selects a candidate version.
Panel shows three prioritized comparisons: latency P50/P95, median token cost delta, and quality delta (eval pass rate on smoke prompt set).
Panel provides an automated "Pin Suggestion" with rationale (e.g., "recommended: v3.2-small-quant — 12% lower P95, +0.3% eval delta; safe for 10% canary").
A short onboarding wizard guides the user through: previewing perf delta, selecting a canary percent, choosing rollback window, and publishing a pin with one-click.
Telemetry events emitted for panel open, suggestion accepted/rejected, and wizard completion so PM can measure time-to-pin and rollback frequency.
Design merges validated in Figma and a developer-ready component spec exists with tokens and interaction states.
design_notes: Primary affordance: small overlay to the right of the version list (not a modal) so users can compare without losing context.
Visual priorities: large, color-coded delta numbers; sparkline for recent latency distribution; subtle heatmap for regional variance.
Use progressive disclosure: top-level three metrics + 'more details' expand to show full profile (memory, quantization settings, kernel hints).
Include explicit confidence badges (data freshness: 2h, sample size: 4k requests) to avoid over-trusting noisy deltas.
Accessibility: keyboard focus lands in the panel when opened; use aria-live for status updates during canary deploy steps.
interaction_flows: Flow A - Quick Pin: User selects version -> Panel opens -> Review top metrics -> Accept suggested pin -> Opens lightweight modal to choose canary percent -> Confirm -> Pin created.
Flow B - Deep Compare: User selects two versions -> Panel shows side-by-side sparklines and per-route breakdown -> User clicks 'Open Full Profile' to go to Performance Snapshot page.
Flow C - Onboard Wizard: New model onboarding triggers a one-time walk-through anchored to the Quick-Compare Panel explaining metrics and safe defaults.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Data freshness may cause incorrect pin suggestions. Mitigation: show freshness badge and fallback to 'manual review required' when sample size < 500.
Risk: Over-simplifying quality into a single metric can mislead. Mitigation: show small eval summary and link to full eval suite with raw examples.
Risk: Private deployments may not expose required telemetry. Mitigation: gate Pin Suggestion feature behind a capability check; show plain panel without automated suggestion for those customers.
open_questions: Should 'Pin Suggestion' consider cost-weighted latency (tokens * ms) or raw P95? PM leaning toward cost-weighted for cost-sensitive customers.
What defaults for canary percent should we recommend for new vs. experienced teams? Suggested defaults: 10% new, 25% experienced.
Do we allow pinning to a quantized variant automatically when it's the suggested candidate? (security/compatibility concern for some customers).
implementation_notes: Front-end: new React component QuickComparePanel with small state machine: closed -> preview -> expanded -> wizard.
Back-end: rely on existing /profiles/delta endpoint; if unavailable, show 'Metrics unavailable' and enable manual comparison.
Telemetry: events: quick_compare.open, quick_compare.suggestion_shown, quick_compare.suggestion_accepted, quick_compare.wizard_completed.
Metrics to track post-launch: time_to_pin (minutes), first_pin_success_rate (no rollback within 48h), suggestion_accept_rate.

notes_for_engineering: Please validate the perf-profile delta API can return 7-day and 1-hour windows to compute both stable and fresh deltas.
If delta endpoint is slow, implement optimistic prefetch on hover with a small debounce (150ms).
Backend should annotate responses with 'capability: suggestion_allowed' for private/on-prem deployments.
